correctness.rationale: All palindromic six-factors must pass through one of four palindrome-center vertices. Two loop-center pairings are impossible, while each of the two nonconstant vertices has a binary direct-versus-crossed transition choice. The degree-two BEST theorem and directed Matrix–Tree theorem show the number of tours with zero, one, or two specified direct pairings equals root Laplacian cofactors 2048,768,768,256. Direct integer determinant computation and a logically independent exhaustive Euler tour enumerator returned exactly the same counts and 2048 complete cycles, with 92636 explored nodes. There are no unproved infinite claims.

value.rationale: Every order-five universal cycle shares exactly the same length-five factor multiset, yet its palindromic length-six factor count depends on pairings of adjacent five-grams. The full three-valued distribution and negative correlation between the two local palindrome-center events quantify a natural new symmetry invariant of de Bruijn cycles. It is a complete exact finite classification in a classical object, with independently reproducible methods. It is not merely recomputation of total cycle count or a claim that finite data implies infinite behavior.
